---
title: "Quiz: Independent units and sampling"
---

[Exercises](14-replicates-uncertainty.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/14-replicates-uncertainty/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** One plant is measured twelve times with a ruler. How many independently
treated plants does this provide? What can the repeated readings help assess?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Separate the unit assigned to treatment from repeated measurement of it.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
**One plant**. The repeats help assess measurement consistency; they do
not create twelve independent plants.
:::

---

**Q2.** Treatment is assigned to whole trays, with twelve plants in each tray.
Which is the treatment unit?

(i) A ruler reading.  

(ii) Each plant independently.  

(iii) A tray.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
All plants in a tray receive the same allocation together.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(iii), a tray. Plants within it share the treatment unit and potentially
the environment. More independently allocated trays are needed for independent
tray-level replication.
:::

---

**Q3.** The supplied simulation draws from one fixed source distribution. Will
means of samples of sixteen usually spread more or less than means of samples
of four? Does the source SD change?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Distinguish variation among observations from variation among estimated means.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The sixteen-draw means usually spread **less**. The stored source values
and their SD stay unchanged.
:::

---

**Q4.** What do the 400 values in `means_16` represent?

(i) 400 newly measured plants.  

(ii) Means of 400 simulated samples, each with sixteen draws.  

(iii) Sixteen means from samples of 400 plants.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Read the outer repetition count and inner sample size separately.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(ii). `replicate(400, mean(sample(..., size = 16, replace = TRUE)))`
calculates 400 means. The draws simulate sampling; they are not new measurements.
:::

---

**Q5.** You increase simulation repetitions from 400 to 1000 while retaining
sixteen draws per sample. Does this have the same effect as increasing plants
per sample? What does `set.seed()` control?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
One setting changes how well the simulated distribution is represented;
the other changes what each estimate averages.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
No. More repetitions give a more stable picture of the same sampling
distribution; more independent draws per mean typically narrow it. `set.seed()`
sets the random generator state so the simulated sequence can be reproduced.
:::
